title: Who sets the rules of the internet? The decisions most users never notice
body:
The multistakeholder approach plays an important role in internet governance, bringing governments, technology companies, technical communities and civil society into decision-making processes.

For example, ICANN coordinates key functions of the domain name system, international technical communities develop standards, governments establish legal requirements, and technology companies implement specific solutions in their products. [...] However, the growth of a national technology industry does not automatically translate into a proportionate influence on international standard-setting.

A country can develop successful digital products while remaining dependent on rules and infrastructure largely shaped beyond its borders.

Another challenge is policy continuity.

Inconsistent policies and weak institutions can mean that progress made under one government stalls when political leadership changes. [...] Sometimes countries have to revisit stages they have already completed.

This is particularly important for international digital governance. Participation in standards development can take years, while shifting government priorities can interrupt the accumulation of expertise and the implementation of decisions already made.

Influence over global digital rules also depends on a country’s ability to build stable institutions capable of representing national interests across political cycles.

title: ​Most Big Tech Partnerships Fail After The Signature

title: Your company needs a new capability. Should you build it, buy it or partner for it? - Fast Company
body: The story pains me to share even now, but it’s one that gets told over and over by other businesses as they wrestle with the decision to build, buy, or partner. Artificial intelligence has accelerated the pace at which businesses can develop new products, enter new markets, and reach new customers. AI also exposes gaps in a company’s capabilities, so leaders are facing the build/buy/partner question more often. Many are defaulting to the wrong decision: build. [...] Now businesses are hampered by AI overconfidence, or a belief that AI can reduce the costs and effort of building in-house. In fact, AI is changing the math, but not evenly. It has made prototypes dramatically cheaper, and the savings are real. But they’re front-loaded. Running a capability, which means maintaining, securing and improving it for years, still takes resources, and AI shrinks those costs far less than it shrinks the cost of a demo. [...] Why does a bias for building in-house persist? The reasons include overconfidence (“I just need four people and six months”), not-invented-here syndrome, and what I refer to as launch bias, or estimating what it takes to launch, not what it takes to run the capability.

title: Brazil's Lula adds pressure on big techs by increasing their liability for illegal user content - Greenwich Time
body: # Brazil's Lula adds pressure on big techs by increasing their liability for illegal user content. SAO PAULO (AP) — Brazil’s President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva signed two decrees on Wednesday that add to the pressure on big tech companies by increasing their liability for illegal content shared by its users and paving the way for investigations by a government body into their responses to such cases. The first decree makes key adaptations to government regulations to align them with a decision by Brazil’s Supreme Court making big tech companies liable if they refuse to remove content by judicial order. Brazil’s government said in a statement that from now on platforms must analyze any complaints, and if the content is deemed criminal, remove it immediately, while communicating the decision to the person responsible. Patricia Peck, a council member of Brazil’s Data Protection Authority and author of 46 books on law and technology, said the country’s executive and judicial branches have pushed for big techs to be proactive against crimes online despite evident stagnation of the debate in congress.
